CJC-1295

CJC-1295 clearly activates the growth-hormone pathway in humans. The bigger question is what that actually translates to.

CJC-1295 is a long-acting analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). Small controlled human studies show sustained increases in growth hormone and IGF-1. That gives the compound a real human biological signal—even though the recovery, body-composition and performance outcomes driving community interest have not been established to the same degree.

In Plain English

CJC-1295 stimulates your body to release more of its own growth hormone and IGF-1, which is why it has become popular for recovery, body composition and performance.

Editorial verdict
Proven hormonal effect.
Promising downstream potential.

The strongest human evidence shows target engagement: CJC-1295 raises GH and IGF-1. Whether that reliably produces the optimization outcomes people seek is the more open question.

Ratings are editorial orientation and should be read alongside the underlying studies, endpoints and regulatory context.
01 / WHAT IT IS

A long-acting signal to the GH axis.

CJC-1295 was designed to extend the action of GHRH and stimulate endogenous growth-hormone secretion for much longer than native GHRH.

The best-known human research studied a DAC form designed to bind to circulating albumin, creating a prolonged pharmacologic effect. That formulation detail matters: products sold or discussed under the broad “CJC-1295” name are not necessarily interchangeable.

The key distinction: CJC-1295 is not simply “growth hormone.” It stimulates the body's GH axis upstream—and human studies demonstrate that biological effect.
02 / HUMAN EVIDENCE

The target engagement is real.

In two randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind ascending-dose trials in healthy adults, a single CJC-1295 administration produced dose-dependent increases in mean GH of roughly 2- to 10-fold for six days or longer and mean IGF-1 of about 1.5- to 3-fold for 9–11 days. After repeated administration, mean IGF-1 remained above baseline for up to 28 days.

A separate human physiology study found that CJC-1295 increased trough and mean GH secretion and IGF-1 while preserving GH pulsatility. That is useful mechanistic evidence because it shows prolonged stimulation did not simply flatten secretion into a constant pattern.

What this supports: sustained GH/IGF-1 stimulation in humans. What remains less answered: how much that translates into clinically meaningful recovery, muscle, fat-loss or performance outcomes.
03 / COMMUNITY SIGNAL

The community is interested in what comes after the lab value.

CJC-1295 has developed a strong optimization identity around recovery, sleep, body composition, training adaptation and GH-axis support.

That interest is understandable: the compound has a demonstrated human hormonal effect, and GH/IGF-1 biology intersects with several outcomes people care about. Community discussion also frequently pairs CJC-1295 with other GH secretagogues such as ipamorelin.

Our read: this is a legitimate emerging signal worth tracking. The community is effectively asking whether a demonstrated endocrine effect produces meaningful real-world benefits that the clinical literature has not yet adequately measured.
04 / CLAIM VS EVIDENCE

Where a real mechanism becomes a bigger promise.

“CJC-1295 raises GH and IGF-1.”Supported. Controlled human studies demonstrated sustained increases in both.
“It preserves natural GH pulses.”Supported by a small human physiology study in healthy men after CJC-1295 administration.
“It improves recovery.”Promising rationale and strong community interest, but recovery itself has not been established as a clinical outcome in controlled CJC-1295 trials.
“It builds muscle and burns fat.”Those claims go beyond the direct CJC-1295 human evidence. Raising GH/IGF-1 is not the same endpoint as demonstrating meaningful changes in muscle mass or adiposity.
“CJC-1295 + ipamorelin is clinically proven.”The combination is prominent in community use, but popularity and complementary mechanistic logic do not substitute for controlled outcome trials of the combination.
05 / THE GAP

MEANINGFUL

Clinical Evidence × Community Signal
MEANINGFUL

The biological effect is not really the mystery. CJC-1295 can meaningfully increase GH and IGF-1 in humans. The unanswered question is how reliably that hormonal change translates into the recovery, body-composition and performance benefits that drive community interest.

06 / SAFETY + REGULATORY

Formulation and product identity matter.

FDA's current compounding safety-risk page states that compounded drugs containing CJC-1295 may pose immunogenicity risks for certain routes and can involve peptide-impurity and active-ingredient characterization complexities. FDA also says available clinical data are limited and identifies serious adverse events associated with CJC-1295, including increased heart rate and a systemic vasodilatory reaction.

In its 2024 review of several CJC-1295-related bulk substances for the 503A Bulks List, FDA emphasized inconsistent naming and characterization, limited clinical safety information, and lack of clinical effectiveness data for the nominated growth-hormone-deficiency use. The advisory committee voted against adding the evaluated CJC-1295 forms to the list.

Regulatory context is not the same as a verdict on the biology. The human GH/IGF-1 findings remain real; FDA's compounding review raises separate questions about specific bulk substances, product characterization, safety and evidence for proposed clinical use.
